title: cymopterus corrugatus var. coulteri
intro: Cymopterus corrugatus var. coulteri, commonly known as Coulteri's desert parsley, is a perennial plant species in the carrot family (Apiaceae). It is native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico, and its roots and leaves have been used in traditional medicine for their health benefits. The plant is believed to have anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, which may provide relief from colds, fever, and skin irritations. The bioactive constituents of Coulteri's desert parsley include volatile oils, alkaloids, and glycosides, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and expectorant properties.
